label: EdgePoint S16
description: EdgePoint S16 (EP-S16) - 16x 1G RJ45 + 2x 10G SFP+ (1/10G). Ports 1-4 source 54V or 24V passive PoE output at 1.4A 4-pair; ports 5-16 source 802.3af/at or 24V/0.7A 2-pair passive PoE. Ports 1 and 2 also accept passive PoE in at 54V/1.5A. 40 W max excluding PoE output; 284 W PoE envelope on the 54 V / 6 A DC input.

poe.note: DERIVED ENVELOPE, not a quoted budget - Ubiquiti prints no "PoE budget" row for this box on either surface. The two figures it does print give the headroom exactly: "Power method (1) DC terminal block, 54V DC, 6A input" = 324 W, and "Max. power consumption 40W (Excludes PoE output)", so at most 324 - 40 = 284 W can leave the sixteen PSE ports on the stated DC-input configuration. Same arithmetic shape as devices/ubiquiti/uisp-r.json and devices/ubiquiti/er-6p.json. A box instead fed by its two 54V/1.5A passive PoE inputs has 2 x 81 = 162 W of input and therefore at most 162 - 40 = 122 W for its own PSE ports; a lab that powers it that way states its own figure. Read 2026-11-19: https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf (HTTP 200, application/pdf, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp; page 9 "Hardware Specifications EP-S16" and page 5 "EP-S16 Bottom Panel") and https://techspecs.ui.com/uisp/wired/ep-s16 (HTTP 200, 577,761 B, rendered spec table, not the 609,911 B front page). NOT a 48 V negotiated standard on ports 1-4: those four are 54V or 24V passive 4-pair (+1, 2, 4, 5; -3, 6, 7, 8) with no 802.3 detection at all, so a 48 V 802.3af/at PD on port 1 will not negotiate - the same defect test/uisp-r-poe.test.js records for the UISP Router. Ports 5-16 are the standards ones: the datasheet names them "PoE/PoE+" and the tech-spec table repeats "(12) PoE/PoE+ or 24V/0.7A".

notes:
Census, all from the vendor datasheet text layer (https://dl.ui.com/datasheets/edgemax/EdgePoint_DS.pdf - 200, 6,571,516 B, 12 pp, "Models: EP-R6, EP-R8, EP-S16", read 2026-11-19) unless stated:

PORTS - page 9: "Data Ports (16) 10/100/1000 RJ45 Ports, (2) 1/10 Gbps SFP+ Ports"; "Serial Console Port (1) RJ45 Serial Port". The console is a line, not a link (research/console-is-a-line-not-an-interface.md), so it is recorded here and not as an interface. Sixteen copper + two cages is what this spec has, and it is the whole of the box.

PoE OUTPUT - page 9: "Passive PoE Output (4) 54V or 24V /1.4A, 4-Pair (+1, 2, 4, 5; -3, 6, 7, 8) Passive PoE, Ports 1 to 4" and "(12) 802.3af/at or 24V/0.7A, 2-Pair (+4, 5; -7, 8) Passive PoE, Ports 5 to 16"; the rendered tech-spec table prints the same second row as "(12) PoE/PoE+ or 24V/0.7A, 2-pair". So ports 1-4 (eth0-eth3) are 54 V or 24 V PASSIVE at 1.4 A - 75.6 W at 54 V, 33.6 W at 24 V - and carry NO 802.3 detection; ports 5-16 (eth4-eth15) are 802.3af/at port when the input is 54 V, with a 24 V/0.7 A passive alternative (16.8 W) when the port is set to 24 V mode.

WHAT WAS WRONG - the row carried no `poe` block at all, so `engine/simulator.js` opened with `if (!dev.poeBudget) continue;` and skipped the box: sixteen PSE ports that could not power a single airMAX radio, with `show power inline` reporting "budget not modelled". The four high-power ports were also labelled `poeOutClass: "PoE"` (802.3af, 48 V negotiated), the exact inversion this catalogue fixed on the UISP Router (see test/uisp-r-poe.test.js): the four ports that are passive 75.6 W ports were filed as the weakest ones, and the twelve af/at ports as the strongest.

PoE INPUT - page 9: "Passive PoE Input (2) 54V /1.5A, 4-Pair ... Ports 1 and 2" with "Do NOT Configure Port 1 or 2 in PoE Output Mode if You Are Using PoE Input Power Sources", and page 5 lists the power inputs as "(1) DC Terminal Block or (2) RJ45 (Ports 1 and 2)". eth0 and eth1 therefore declare `poeIn: 40` - the vendor's own "Max. power consumption 40W (Excludes PoE output)" is what the box draws from a PoE source; the 1.5 A row is the port's input capacity, not a draw, and is not used as one.

NOT MODELLED - the box is a layer-2 switch with some layer-3 capability (datasheet page 2: "EP-S16 Layer-2 switch with some layer-3 capabilities", "Static Routing, Policy-Based Routing" on page 3), so `l2-forward` is declared alongside `l3-forward`; no 802.3bt, no PoE++ capability and no slot census are claimed, because the datasheet prints none.
